Below is a quick‑reference guide for pulling “detailed” information about a network interface on the three most common operating systems.  
If you’re looking for something more specific (e.g., a particular API call, a library, or a custom script), just let me know and I’ll dive deeper into that angle.

## 1️⃣ Linux / Unix‑like Systems  

| Tool | What it gives you | Typical usage |
|------|-------------------|---------------|
| **`ip link show <iface>`** | Basic link state, MTU, flags, MAC address | `ip link show eth0` |
| **`ip -s link show <iface>`** | Same as above + per‑direction packet/byte counters | `ip -s link show eth0` |
| **`ip -details link show <iface>`** | Adds driver name, speed, duplex, link mode, etc. | `ip -details link show eth0` |
| **`ethtool <iface>`** | Driver info, supported speeds, current speed/duplex, autoneg status, driver module, firmware version | `ethtool eth0` |
| **`ethtool -S <iface>`** | Raw statistics counters (bytes, packets, errors, drops) | `ethtool -S eth0` |
| **`ethtool -i <iface>`** | Driver/module info (driver name, version, firmware, bus info) | `ethtool -i eth0` |
| **`ethtool -a <iface>`** | Autonegotiation settings | `ethtool -a eth0` |
| **`ethtool -m <iface>`** | EEPROM contents (useful for firmware checks) | `ethtool -m eth0` |
| **`ethtool -T <iface>`** | Link partner capabilities (speed, duplex, autoneg) | `ethtool -T eth0` |
| **`ethtool -p <iface>`** | Blink LEDs (for troubleshooting) | `ethtool -p eth0` |
| **`ethtool -G <iface> rx <size>`** | Adjust RX/TX ring buffer sizes | `ethtool -G eth0 rx 4096` |
| **`ethtool -K <iface> tx off`** | Disable/enable features (e.g., TX checksum offload) | `ethtool -K eth0 tx off` |
| **`ethtool -r <iface>`** | Reset NIC | `ethtool -r eth0` |
| **`ethtool -V <iface>`** | Firmware version | `ethtool -V eth0` |
| **`ethtool -c <iface>`** | Current coalescing settings | `ethtool -c eth0` |
| **`ethtool -C <iface> rx-usecs 100`** | Set coalescing parameters | `ethtool -C eth0 rx-usecs 100` |
| **`ethtool -N <iface> flow-type udp4 dst-port 53`** | Flow director rules | `ethtool -N eth0 flow-type udp4 dst-port 53` |
| **`ethtool -n <iface> rx-flowid 0`** | Flow ID mapping | `ethtool -n eth0 rx-flowid 0` |
| **`ethtool -t <iface>`** | Run diagnostics test | `ethtool -t eth0` |
| **`ethtool -v <iface>`** | Verbose output (debugging) | `ethtool -v eth0` |

| **`ethtool -P <iface>`** | Permanent MAC address | `ethtool -P eth0` |

### Quick “All‑in‑one” command

```bash
# Show everything you can get from ethtool in one shot
sudo ethtool -i eth0 && \
sudo ethtool -a eth0 && \
sudo ethtool -G eth0 && \
sudo ethtool -S eth0 && \
sudo ethtool -T eth0 && \
sudo ethtool -c eth0 && \
sudo ethtool -k eth0
```

### Programmatic access

* **Netlink sockets** (`libnl`, `pyroute2`) – read the `IFLA_*` attributes.  
* **SNMP** – walk the IF-MIB (`ifDescr`, `ifType`, `ifSpeed`, `ifPhysAddress`, `ifOperStatus`, etc.).  
* **sysfs** – `/sys/class/net/<iface>/` contains many files: `address`, `operstate`, `speed`, `duplex`, `tx_queue_len`, `statistics/*`, `device/...`.  
* **udev** – `udevadm info --query=property --name=<iface>` gives driver/module info.

---

## 2️⃣ Windows (PowerShell)

| Cmdlet | What it gives you | Example |
|--------|-------------------|---------|
| **`Get-NetAdapter -Name "<iface>"`** | Basic adapter properties (status, MAC, speed, duplex, driver, etc.) | `Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet` |
| **`Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias "<iface>"`** | IP config (IPv4/IPv6 addresses, DNS, gateway) | `Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias Ethernet` |
| **`Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name "<iface>"`** | Advanced properties (e.g., RSS, JUMBO frames) | `Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name Ethernet` |
| **`Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name "<iface>"`** | Packet/byte counters, error counts | `Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name Ethernet` |
| **`Get-NetAdapterBinding -Name "<iface>"`** | Protocol bindings (TCP/IP, IPv6, etc.) | `Get-NetAdapterBinding -Name Ethernet` |
| **`Get-NetAdapterHardwareInfo -Name "<iface>"`** | Hardware info (PCI bus, vendor, device IDs) | `Get-NetAdapterHardwareInfo -Name Ethernet` |
| **`Get-NetAdapter -Name "<iface>" | Format-List *`** | Full object dump (all properties) | `Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet | Format-List *` |

### Using WMI (classic)

```powershell
Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapter -Filter "NetConnectionID='Ethernet'" | Select-Object *
```

### Programmatic (C#, .NET)

```csharp
var adapters = System.Net.NetworkInformation.NetworkInterface.GetAllNetworkInterfaces();
foreach (var ni in adapters)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{ni.Name}: {ni.Description}");
    Console.WriteLine($"  Status: {ni.OperationalStatus}");
    Console.WriteLine($"  Speed: {ni.Speed / 1_000_000} Mbps");
    Console.WriteLine($"  MAC: {ni.GetPhysicalAddress()}");
}
```

---

## 3️⃣ macOS

| Command | What it gives you | Example |
|---------|-------------------|---------|
| **`ifconfig <iface>`** | Interface state, MAC, MTU, flags, IP addresses | `ifconfig en0` |
| **`networksetup -getinfo <iface>`** | DHCP lease info, DNS servers, router | `networksetup -getinfo Wi-Fi` |
| **`networksetup -getmacaddress <iface>`** | Physical MAC address | `networksetup -getmacaddress Wi-Fi` |
| **`networksetup -getairportpower <iface>`** | Wireless power state | `networksetup -getairportpower en0` |
| **`networksetup -getairportnetwork <iface>`** | Current SSID | `networksetup -getairportnetwork en0` |
| **`networksetup -listallhardwareports`** | Map between hardware port names and BSD device names | `networksetup -listallhardwareports` |
| **`netstat -i`** | Interface statistics (packets, errors, collisions) | `netstat -i` |
| **`netstat -I <iface> -f inet`** | Per‑interface IPv4 stats | `netstat -I en0 -f inet` |
| **`netstat -I <iface> -f inet6`** | Per‑interface IPv6 stats | `netstat -I en0 -f inet6` |
| **`sysctl -a | grep <iface>`** | Kernel tunables related to the interface | `sysctl -a | grep en0` |
| **`dmesg | grep <iface>`** | Kernel messages for the interface | `dmesg | grep en0` |

### Programmatic (Swift / Objective‑C)

```swift
import SystemConfiguration
import Network

// Get all interfaces
var ifaddr : UnsafeMutablePointer<ifaddrs>? = nil
if getifaddrs(&ifaddr) == 0 {
    var ptr = ifaddr
    while ptr != nil {
        let interface = ptr!.pointee
        let name = String(cString: interface.ifa_name!)
        print("Interface: \(name)")
        ptr = interface.ifa_next
    }
    freeifaddrs(ifaddr)
}
```

---

## 4️⃣ Cross‑Platform SNMP (if you have an agent)

```bash
snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifTable
```

Typical OIDs:

| OID | Meaning | Example |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.<index>` | `ifDescr` – description | `eth0` |
| `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5.<index>` | `ifSpeed` – speed (bits/s) | `1000000000` |
| `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.7.<index>` | `ifAdminStatus` – admin state | `up(1)` |
| `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.<index>` | `ifOperStatus` – operational state | `up(1)` |
| `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.14.<index>` | `ifInOctets` – inbound bytes | `123456789` |
| `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.20.<index>` | `ifOutOctets` – outbound bytes | `987654321` |
| `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.16.<index>` | `ifInErrors` – inbound errors | `0` |
| `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.22.<index>` | `ifOutErrors` – outbound errors | `0` |

## 5️⃣ Summary Cheat Sheet

| OS | One‑liner for “everything” |
|----|-----------------------------|
| **Linux** | `sudo ethtool -i eth0 && sudo ethtool -a eth0 && sudo ethtool -G eth0 && sudo ethtool -S eth0 && sudo ethtool -T eth0 && sudo ethtool -c eth0 && sudo ethtool -k eth0` |
| **Windows** | `Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet | Format-List *` |
| **macOS** | `ifconfig en0 && networksetup -getinfo Wi-Fi && netstat -i` |

3. If you’re dealing with a *specific* device type (e.g., a Cisco switch, a Juniper router, a VMware ESXi host), let me know and I can point you at the exact CLI commands or APIs for that environment.

Happy querying!
